metadata.remarks:
Resolved profile catalog: the CSCS catalog reduced to the 39 controls the `high-impact-csc` profile chain selects. Section groups left with no controls are removed; the front-matter groups and the back-matter are kept whole.

Generated from the NCSA's published PDF by `pdf_to_catalog.py`. The framework content is the National Cyber Security Committee's; the OSCAL rendering is not theirs and they have not reviewed it, which is why the parties above describe the source document and no party is named as an author of this catalog.

The source is an unofficial English translation. Clause 5 was retranslated between version 1.0 and version 1.1 — same 41 clauses and the same clause 4 matrix, substantially different English — so `metadata.version` is the *translation* version, not a version of the standard.

Each clause of the standard is two controls, one per party column, suffixed `-csc` and `-csp`. Six clauses address one party only and mint one control. Sections carry `props[name=minimum-impact-level]`, the weakest impact level at which the clause 4 matrix requires them.

parts.name: provision
parts.title: Clause 1
parts.prose: This notification shall be called the Notification of the National Cyber Security Committee Re: Cybersecurity Standards for Cloud Systems, B.E. 2567 (2024)."

parts.name: provision
parts.title: Clause 2
parts.prose: This notification shall come into force two years after its publication in the Royal Thai Government Gazette.

parts.name: provision
parts.title: Clause 3
parts.prose: In this notification: "Agency" refers to government agencies, regulators, and organizations of critical information infrastructure as defined by the Cybersecurity Act, B.E. 2562 (2019). "Cloud Computing" refers to the concept of accessing information networks consisting of shareable, elastic, and scalable physical or virtual resources through self-service provisioning and on-demand administration. "Cloud Service" refers to the capability to perform cloud computing, which is accessible via a designated interface. "Cloud Service Category" refers to a group of cloud services with certain shared characteristics, categorized as follows: (1) Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): Comprising computing systems, data storage, networks, and other relevant resources, where users can efficiently use software on provided infrastructure without managing the underlying infrastructure. (2) Platform as a Service (PaaS): Comprising application platforms, databases, and computer services, where users can develop, deploy, and configure software without managing the underlying infrastructure. (3) Software as a Service (SaaS): Where providers offer ready-to-use software, and users manage configurations, parameters, processing units, and storage to achieve their service objectives. (4) Any combination of services from (1) to (3). (5) Other services as notified by the Office. "Public Cloud" refers to cloud services accessible by any cloud service user, with resources controlled by the cloud service provider. "Cloud Service Customer" (CSC) refers to an agency with a formal contract to use cloud services provided by a cloud service provider. "Cloud Service Provider" (CSP) refers to a public or private entity that makes cloud services available to customers, managing resources to ensure availability, security, and scalability for its users. "Personal Data" refers to personal data as defined in Section 6 of the Personal Data Protection Act, B.E. 2562 (2019). "Office" refers to the Office of the National Cyber Security Agency.

parts.name: provision
parts.title: Clause 4
parts.prose: Agencies using public cloud services must comply with this standard, taking into account the impact level of data or information systems as specified in the Notification of the National Cyber Security Committee Re: Standards for Cybersecurity Categorization of Data or Information Systems, B.E. 2566 (2023), and must meet at least the minimum requirements set out at the end of this notification.

parts.name: provision
parts.title: Clause 5
parts.prose: For personal data, the impact level for confidentiality must be classified at least as medium, as specified in the Notification of the National Cyber Security Committee Re: Standards for Cybersecurity Categorization of Data or Information Systems, B.E. 2566 (2023), and must meet at least the minimum requirements set out at the end of this notification.

parts.name: provision
parts.title: Clause 6
parts.prose: Agencies must submit a summary report of the actions taken to the Office within 30 days of completion.

parts.name: provision
parts.title: Clause 7
parts.prose: The Secretary-General of the National Cyber Security Committee is responsible for enforcing this notification and is authorized to issue notifications, orders, criteria, and procedures to comply with this notification. In case of any issues related to compliance with this notification or matters not specified herein, the Chairman of the National Cyber Security Committee shall have the authority to interpret and adjudicate, and such interpretation and decision shall be final. Given on 10 September B.E. 2567 (2024) Phumtham Wechayachai Deputy Prime Minister as Chairman of the National Cyber Security Committee

parts.name: certification
parts.title: Low Impact — Cloud Service Customer
parts.prose: Self-assessment along with supporting documentation and approval from the highest executive of the organization, the assessment must be retained by the organization and submitted to the office

parts.name: certification
parts.title: Low Impact — Cloud Service Provider
parts.prose: Certified by certify bodies on a 3-year cycle, consisting of certification the 1st year and surveillance audits in the 2nd and 3rd years, certification must also be certified to at least ISO/IEC 27001 and CSA STAR Level 1/CCM Lite.

parts.name: certification
parts.title: Moderate Impact — Cloud Service Customer
parts.prose: Certified by the regulators (Attestation) or certified by a certify body on a 3-year cycle. This includes a full certification in the 1st year and a surveillance audit in the 2nd and 3rd years.

parts.name: certification
parts.title: Moderate Impact — Cloud Service Provider
parts.prose: Certified by a certify body on a 3-year cycle. This includes a full certification in the 1st year and a surveillance audit in the 2nd and 3rd years. Additionally, it must also be certified at least to CSA STAR Level 2/CCM and ISO/IEC 27701.

parts.name: minimum-requirements
parts.title: High Impact — minimum requirements
parts.prose: Part One: - All Part Two: - All

parts.name: certification
parts.title: High Impact — Cloud Service Customer
parts.prose: Certified by a certify body on a 3-year cycle. This includes a full certification in the 1st year and a surveillance audit in the 2nd and 3rd years

parts.name: certification
parts.title: High Impact — Cloud Service Provider
parts.prose: Certified by a certify body on a 3-year cycle. This includes a full certification in the 1st year and a surveillance audit in the 2nd and 3rd years. Additionally, it must also be certified to either ISO/IEC 27017 or CSA STAR Level 2/CCM, and ISO/IEC 27018 and ISO/IEC 27701.

controls.title: Information Security Policies (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: An information security policy for cloud computing shall be defined as a topic-specific policy of the cloud service customer. The cloud service customer's information security policy for cloud computing shall be consistent with the organization's acceptable levels of information security risks for its information and other assets.

parts.name: item
item
parts.prose: The personal data protection policy shall be augmented by a statement concerning support for and commitment to achieving compliance with applicable personal data protection legislation and the contractual terms agreed between the cloud service provider and the cloud service customer.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Contractual agreements shall clearly allocate responsibilities between the cloud service provider, its sub-contractors and the cloud service customer, taking into account the type of cloud service in question (e.g. a service of an IaaS, PaaS or SaaS category of the cloud computing reference architecture). For example, the allocation of responsibility for application layer controls can differ depending on whether the cloud service provider is providing a SaaS service or rather is providing a PaaS or IaaS service on which the cloud service customer can build or layer its own applications.

controls.title: Information Security Roles and Responsibilities (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall agree with the cloud service provider on an appropriate allocation of information security roles and responsibilities, and confirm that it can fulfil its allocated roles and responsibilities. The information security roles and responsibilities of both parties shall be stated in an agreement.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall identify and manage its relationship with the customer support and care function of the customer cloud service provider.

controls.title: Contact with Authorities (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall identify the authorities relevant to the combined operation of the cloud service customer and the cloud service provider.

controls.title: Identification of Applicable Legislation and Contractual Requirements (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall consider the issue that relevant laws and regulations can be those of jurisdictions governing the cloud service provider, in addition to those governing the cloud service customer.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall request evidence of the cloud service provider's compliance with relevant regulations and standards required for the cloud service customer's business. Such evidence can be the certifications produced by third-party auditors.

controls.title: Intellectual Property Rights (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Installing commercially licensed software in a cloud service can cause a breach of the license terms for the software. The cloud service customer shall have a procedure for identifying cloud-specific licensing requirements before permitting any licensed software to be installed in a cloud service. Particular attention shall be paid to cases where the cloud service is elastic and scalable and the software can be run on more systems or processor cores than is permitted by the license terms.

controls.title: Protection of Records (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall request information from the cloud service provider about the protection of records gathered and stored by the cloud service provider that are relevant to the use of cloud services by the cloud service customer.

controls.title: Regulation of Cryptographic Controls (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall verify that the set of cryptographic controls that apply to the use of a cloud service comply with relevant agreements, legislation and regulations.

controls.title: Independent Review of Information Security (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall request documented evidence that the implementation of information security controls and guidelines for the cloud service is in line with any claims made by the cloud service provider. Such evidence could include certifications against relevant standards.

groups.title: Part Two: Cloud Infrastructure Security and Operation

controls.title: Information Security Awareness, Education and Training (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
item
parts.prose: Information security awareness, education and training programmes about cloud services shall be provided to management and the supervising managers, including those of business units.

controls.title: Inventory of Assets (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer's inventory of assets shall account for information and associated assets stored in the cloud computing environment. The records of the inventory should indicate where the assets are maintained, e.g., identification of the cloud service.

controls.title: Labelling of Information (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall label information and associated assets maintained in the cloud computing environment in accordance with the cloud service customer's adopted procedures for labelling.

controls.title: Access to Networks and Network Services (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer's access control policy for the use of network services shall specify requirements for user access to each separate cloud service that is used.

controls.title: User Registration and Deregistration (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Procedures for user registration and de- registration shall address the situation where user access control is compromised, such as the corruption or compromise of passwords or other user registration data (e.g. as a result of inadvertent disclosure).

controls.title: Management of Privileged Access Rights (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall use sufficient authentication techniques (e.g., multi-factor authentication) for authenticating the cloud service administrators of the cloud service customer to the administrative capabilities of a cloud service according to the identified risks.

controls.title: Management of Secret Authentication Information of Users (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall verify that the cloud service provider's management procedure for allocating secret authentication information, such as passwords, meets the cloud service customer's requirements.

controls.title: Information Access Restriction (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall ensure that access to information in the cloud service can be restricted in accordance with its access control policy and that such restrictions are realized. This includes restricting access to cloud services, cloud service functions, and cloud service customer data maintained in the service.

controls.title: Use of Privilege Utility Programs (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where the use of utility programs is permitted, the cloud service customer shall identify the utility programs to be used in its cloud computing environment, and ensure that they do not interfere with the controls of the cloud service.

controls.title: Secure Log-on Procedures (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Cloud service customers shall require users under their control to follow secure log-on procedures for any account.

controls.title: Policy on the Use of Cryptographic Controls (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall implement cryptographic controls for its use whether those controls are supplied by the cloud service customer or by the cloud service provider.

parts.name: item

controls.title: Key Management (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall identify the cryptographic keys for each cloud service, and implement procedures for key management.

parts.name: item
item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall not permit the cloud service provider to store and manage the encryption keys for cryptographic operations when the cloud service customer employs its own key management.

controls.title: Data Center Location (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Shall use primary data centers located in Thailand.

controls.title: Secure Disposal of Reuse of Equipment (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall request confirmation that the cloud service provider has the policies and procedures for secure disposal or reuse of resources.

controls.title: Change Management (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer's change management process shall take into account the impact of any changes made by the cloud service provider.

controls.title: Capacity Management (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall ensure that the agreed capacity provided by the cloud service meets the cloud service customer's requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall monitor the use of cloud services, and forecast resource capacity needs, to ensure performance of the cloud services over time.

controls.title: Information Backup (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where the cloud service provider provides backup capability as part of the cloud service, the cloud service customer shall request the specifications of the backup capability from the cloud service provider. The cloud service customer shall also verify that they meet their backup requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer is responsible for implementing backup capabilities when the cloud service provider does not provide them.

controls.title: Event Logging (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall define its requirements for event logging and verify that the cloud service meets those requirements.

controls.title: Protection of Log Information (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Log information recorded for purposes such as security monitoring and operational diagnostics can contain personal data. Measures, such as controlling access, shall be put in place to ensure that logged information is only used for its intended purposes.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: A procedure, preferably automatic, shall be put in place to ensure that logged information is deleted within a specified retention and documented period.

controls.title: Administrator and Operator Logs (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: If a privileged operation is delegated to the cloud service customer, the operation and performance of those operations shall be logged. The cloud service customer shall determine whether logging capabilities provided by the cloud service provider are appropriate or whether the cloud service customer shall implement additional logging capabilities.

controls.title: Clock Synchronization (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall request information about the clock synchronization used for the cloud service provider's systems.

controls.title: Management of Technical Vulnerabilities (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall request information from the cloud service provider about the management of technical vulnerabilities that can affect the cloud services provided. The cloud service customer shall identify the technical vulnerabilities it will be responsible to manage, and clearly define a process for managing them.

controls.title: Separation of Development, Testing and Operational Environments (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Where the use of personal data for testing purposes cannot be avoided, a risk assessment shall be undertaken. Technical and organizational measures shall be implemented to minimize the risk identified.

controls.title: Information Transfer Policies and Procedures (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Whenever physical media are used for information transfer, a system shall be put in place to record incoming and outgoing physical media containing personal data, including the type of physical media, the authorized sender/recipients, the date and time, and the number of physical media

parts.name: item
parts.prose: Cloud service customer shall request cloud service providers to put additional measures in place (such as encryption) to ensure that data can only be accessed at the point of destination and not in transit.

controls.title: Segregation of Networks (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall defines its requirements for segregating networks to achieve tenant isolation in the shared environment of a cloud service and verify that the cloud service provider meets those requirements.

controls.title: Information Security Requirements Analysis and Specification (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall determine its information security requirements for the cloud service and then evaluate whether services offered by a cloud service provider can meet these requirements.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: For this evaluation, the cloud service customer must request information on the information security capabilities from the cloud service provider.

controls.title: Secure Development Policy (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer must request information from the cloud service provider about the cloud service provider's use of secure development procedures and practices.

controls.title: Information Security Policy for Supplier Relationships (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall include the cloud service provider as a type of supplier in its information security policy for supplier relationships. This will help to mitigate risks associated with the cloud service provider's access to and management of the cloud service customer data.

controls.title: Addressing Security within Supplier Agreements (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item

controls.title: Responsibilities and Procedures (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
parts.prose: The cloud service customer shall verify the allocation of responsibilities for information security incident management and shall ensure that it meets the requirements of the cloud service customer.

parts.name: item
parts.prose: An information security incident shall trigger a review by the cloud service customer, or jointly between the cloud service customer and the cloud service provider, as part of their information security incident management process, to determine whether a personal data breach has occurred.

controls.title: Reporting Information Security Events (Cloud Service Customer)

parts.name: item
